violated_contract: A read that selects a Firestore field mask and then applies a shared visibility predicate in Python must select every field that predicate reads. A field outside the mask comes back absent, and the predicate reads an absent hide flag as visible, so the projected reader shows rows that every full-document reader hides, with no error. Dream's merge_conversations cleanup (#21480) folds a duplicate capture by writing dream_duplicate_of, which is_visible_conversation hides; the row stays discarded == False, so only that check can hide it. MCP_CONVERSATION_CARD_FIELD_PATHS predates the field and never selected it, so the hosted MCP get_conversations tool, GET /v1/mcp/conversations, the Developer API card list and projected search hydration returned both captures, while the app list and the Developer API transcript path hid the duplicate.
canonical_prevention: Select the visibility predicate's inputs in every field mask that feeds it, and drive each projected reader with a fake that applies the mask the way Firestore does. A fake that returns whole documents passes even when the mask drops a hide flag; a masking fake shows the hidden row coming back.
